description: Text template, number format and plural cases shared by every HotLayout reader (schema 9.4.0). A row is one string value of a document (`value`: a `literal`, a `binding` or a `template`) and everything a reader needs to turn it into text: `sourceLocale` is `localization.defaultLocale` (null: the document has no localization), `translationLocale` is the `translation` answer of locale resolution (the key of `localization.strings` the reader uses; equal to `sourceLocale` when the source language is shown), `formattingLocale` is its `formatting` answer, `translations` holds the entries of `localization.strings[translationLocale]` for this value keyed by the path INSIDE the value (`template`, `values.<name>.forms.<category>`; the empty key is the literal itself), `data` maps data paths to values (a missing key and null are both `no data`), `now` is the reader clock and `timeZone` the device zone (absent: any). The reader must produce `expected` exactly, character for character; U+00A0 is written as an escape. `mayDiffer` marks a row whose answer depends on the CLDR data of the platform: the rule is fixed, the exact characters are not promised, and the note says what may differ. `readerOnly` marks a row with a value the builder cannot produce (the validator or the schema rejects it): it is a rule for readers that meet a document from another producer or a newer minor. Rows named CLARIFIED were added after the first readers were built; rows named CLARIFIED-2, before 9.5.0 was released. Clarification of 9.18.0: `shownTextCases` (a string and the string a reader SHOWS: runs of space, tab, LF and CR become one space, the edges are trimmed, U+00A0 stays) and `shownTemplateCases` (the same rule after the template and the translation: `expected` is the string of the pipeline BEFORE the rule, `shown` after it); the rows of `cases` do not know the rule. The rows `CLARIFIED-3 dateTime` fix the separator between the date and the time (the CLDR pattern of the language, not a space).

moneyNote: Schema 9.19.0 — money as money: the fields «currencyDisplay», «currencyPosition» and «sign» of a binding (rules: x-money). A row of «moneyCases» is a row of «cases» plus «direction»: the direction of the SHOWN text (that of «directionLocale» of locale resolution) — the reader wraps the composed form in U+2066 … U+2069 exactly when it is «rtl». «expected» is the whole string, character for character; U+00A0, U+2066, U+2069 and U+2212 are written as escapes. «pieces» (where present, for a value that is a single binding) are the pieces of the formatted value in logical order, each with «part»: «fraction», «currency» or null for the rest; joined, the pieces are «expected», and the isolation marks sit inside the first and the last piece. A reader of 9.18 fails the rows that name one of the three fields and passes the rows marked WITHOUT.

datePartsNote: Schema 9.19.0 — parts of a date: the field «dateParts» of a binding beside «format: date» (rules: x-dateParts). countdownNote: Schema 9.21.0 — a countdown part: «format: countdownPart» with «unit» (days, hours 0–23, minutes 0–59, seconds 0–59) and an optional «pad: 2» (rules: x-countdown). A row of «countdownCases» is a row of «cases»: «now» is the clock of the reader, the moment is in the data. S = floor(max(0, moment - now) / 1000); the parts round DOWN. «expected» is the whole string, character for character. «readerOnly» — a document the builder does not make, and the row says what a reader does with it.

compactNote: Schema 9.23.0 — a compact number: «notation: compact» beside «format: number» (rules: x-compactNumber). A row of «compactCases» is a row of «cases». Below 1 000 the number is written as «number» writes it; otherwise the magnitude divided by the largest step not above it (thousand, million, billion), one fraction digit, half up (the magnitude, so a negative number rounds away from zero), the trailing zero dropped, a mantissa that reaches 1 000 written with the next step. The suffix comes from a closed table by the first subtag of the formatting locale — «en»: K, M, B with no gap; «uk»: «тис.», «млн», «млрд» after U+00A0; any other language: the «en» suffixes. The decimal separator and the digits are those of the formatting locale. A plural word agrees with the FULL value. «expected» is the whole string, character for character; U+00A0, U+2066, U+2069 and U+2212 are written as escapes.
